Geasey Trophy]] winner ([[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2011]]) *2× First-team All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference|Atlantic 10]] ([[2009–10 Atlantic 10 Conference men's basketball season|2010]], [[2010–11 Atlantic 10 Conference men's basketball season|2011]]) *Third-team All-Atlantic 10 (2009) }} '''Lavoy Allen''' (born February 4, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was selected in the second round, 50th overall pick in the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Allen is the son of a truck driver, and did not play much basketball until eighth grade. He attended [[Pennsbury High School]], where he was coached by Oliver Aaron. [[Rivals.com]] ranked him the 14th best center in his class, and [[Scout.com]] named him the 110th overall prospect. Allen committed to [[Temple University]] and coach [[Fran Dunphy]]. Temple reached the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] in all four seasons that Allen played there. He was a three-time All-Atlantic 10 Defensive Team honoree and a two-time All-Atlantic 10 First Team recipient. In his junior year, he became the first Temple player to average a double-double since [[Ollie Johnson (basketball, born 1949)|Ollie Johnson]] accomplished the feat in 1970–71. Allen declared for early entry in the [[2010 NBA draft]], but withdrew prior to the May 8 deadline. As a senior, Allen surpassed [[Johnny Baum]] as the all-time leading rebounder in Temple history. He was the recipient of the [[Robert V. Geasey Trophy]] honoring the [[Philadelphia Big Five]] Player of the Year. Dunphy has said that Allen "might be the smartest player I've ever coached." ==Early life== Allen was born in [[Trenton, New Jersey]] on February 4, 1989.{{cite news|url=http://articles.philly.com/2011-08-08/news/29864649_1_basketball-clinics-pennsbury-nba-game|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120103215528/http://articles.philly.com/2011-08-08/news/29864649_1_basketball-clinics-pennsbury-nba-game|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 3, 2012|title=Bound by basketball|first=Michael|last=Vitez|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=August 8, 2011|access-date=August 1, 2011}}{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/home/playerfile/lavoy_allen/|title=Lavoy Allen Info Page|work=[[NBA]]|publisher=NBA Media Ventures|access-date=July 20, 2011}} His mother is Paula Allen and his father, Dave Allen, is a truck driver.{{cite news|url=http://articles.philly.com/2010-03-09/sports/24956726_1_tom-gola-arena-high-post-owls-assistant-coach|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120609120614/http://articles.philly.com/2010-03-09/sports/24956726_1_tom-gola-arena-high-post-owls-assistant-coach|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 9, 2012|title=Lavoy Allen taking Temple to new heights|first=Mike|last=Jensen|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=March 9, 2010|access-date=December 24, 2010}} When he was nine years old, Lavoy moved to [[Morrisville, Bucks County, Pennsylvania|Morrisville, Pennsylvania]], and struggled to make friends in his new surroundings. He did not play much organized basketball until eighth grade. In an interview, Allen admitted he was not very good in the beginning, and focused on passing the ball to a better teammate. His initial motivation was how schoolchildren mocked him for his height yet not being able to dunk.{{cite news|url=http://articles.philly.com/2011-01-31/sports/27092178_1_middle-school-frank-sciolla-voluntary-workouts|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130131053324/http://articles.philly.com/2011-01-31/sports/27092178_1_middle-school-frank-sciolla-voluntary-workouts|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 31, 2013|title=Temple's Lavoy Allen has quietly had a spectacular career|first=Dick|last=Jerardi|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=January 31, 2011|access-date=June 5, 2011}} "I could barely jump over the Sunday paper," he said.{{cite news|last1=Woods|first1=David|title=Skills arrived slowly for once-clumsy Lavoy Allen|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2014/02/27/skills-arrived-slowly-for-once-clumsy-lavoy-allen/5883611/|access-date=July 22, 2014|work=[[Indianapolis Star]]|date=February 27, 2014}} ==High school career== He attended [[Pennsbury High School]], where he was coached by Frank Sciolla. Former [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]] player Dalton Pepper was his high school teammate.{{cite news|url=http://www.buckslocalnews.com/articles/2011/06/02/bucks_sports/doc4de7e696b52c3746190495.txt|title=Levittown's Dalton Pepper has transferred to Temple University|first=Steve|last=Sherman|work=[[Bucks Local News]]|date=June 2, 2011|access-date=June 5, 2011}} In ninth grade, Allen decided that he wanted to be great, and put in much more practice time. He became a starter on the varsity team in his sophomore year. As a junior, he averaged 12 [[point (basketball)|point]]s and nine [[rebound (basketball)|rebound]]s per game, and was named a Top 150 player in his class by Hoop Scoop.{{cite web|url=http://www.owlsports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4594&path=mbball|title=2010-11 Men's Basketball Roster: #24 Lavoy Allen|work=[[Temple Owls]]|publisher=[[Temple University]]|access-date=December 25, 2010}} In his senior season, Allen posted per-game averages of 13 points, 9.6 rebounds, 3.2 [[assist (basketball)|assist]]s, 3 [[block (basketball)|block]]s, and 2 [[steal (basketball)|steal]]s. Under Allen, Pennsbury reached the second round of the [[Pennsylvania Interscholastic Athletic Association|PIAA]] playoffs before losing to [[Harrisburg High School (Pennsylvania)|Harrisburg High School]].{{cite news|title=Allen to try out for Team USA |first=Jason|last=Haslem|work=[[Bucks County Courier Times]]|date=June 9, 2007}} He was named to the Second Team all-Southeastern Pennsylvania at the conclusion of the season. Allen tried out for the USA U-19 basketball team, but did not make the final cut. [[Rivals.com]] ranked him the 14th best center in his class, and [[Scout.com]] named him the 110th overall prospect. He worked at a day care facility to earn enough money to bring his date to the [[senior prom]]. On November 8, 2006, Allen committed to Temple, over Division I scholarship offers from [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]], [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's]], and [[La Salle Explorers men's basketball|La Salle]].{{cite news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-154062540.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105065042/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-154062540.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=November selected to the Preseason All-Atlantic 10 Rookie Team.{{cite web|url=http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102407aaa.html|title=Xavier Tabbed To Capture A-10 Men's Basketball Title|work=[[Atlantic 10 Conference]]|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|date=October 24, 2007|access-date=December 26, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728094031/http://www.atlantic10.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/102407aaa.html|archive-date=July 28, 2011|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}} He was seen as an answer for Temple's rebounding and interior scoring struggles from the previous 12–18 season.{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/11/11/sports/ncaabasketball/11temple.html?ref=ncaabasketball|title=High-Scoring Temple Seeks Defensive Edge|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=November 11, 2007|access-date=December 26, 2010}} In his first college basketball game, Allen scored eight points and grabbed nine rebounds in a loss to #7 [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee]]. From November 18 through December 9, 2007, he scored in double figures in six consecutive games. On February 10, 2008, Allen's season-high 20 points led Temple to an 80–70 overtime victory over the [[UMass Minutemen men's basketball|UMass Minutemen]].{{cite news|url=https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280410218|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102233811/https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=280410218|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 2, 2013|title=Temple 80, Massachusetts 70|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 10, 2008|access-date=December 26, 2010}} Allen was benched in the February 17 game against [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] due to missing a study assignment.{{cite news|url=http://articles.philly.com/2008-02-17/sports/25266007_1_temple-ranks-owls-lavoy-allen|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130630034810/http://articles.philly.com/2008-02-17/sports/25266007_1_temple-ranks-owls-lavoy-allen|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 30, 2013|title=Benched player and botched D hurt Owls|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|date=February 17, 2008|access-date=December 28, 2010}} The Owls finished the season 21–13, and made the [[2008 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] for the first time since 2001, receiving a 12 seed by the selection committee. In the first round, they bowed out to fifth-seeded [[2007-08 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] 72–61.{{cite news|url=https://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=284000019|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715103951/https://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=284000019|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 15, 2012|title=Michigan State's wealth of balance puts Temple on ice|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 20, 2008|access-date=December 27, 2010}} In that game, Allen notched his first [[double-double]] of 13 points and 11 rebounds, and also drained his first two collegiate [[three-pointers]]. He led the team in blocks with a total of 52, and finished second in field goal percentage (.558), third in rebounds per game (5.7), and fourth in points per game (8.1). Allen was selected to the All-Atlantic 10 Rookie Team. ===Sophomore=== As a sophomore, Allen increased his scoring average to 10.9 points per game, second on the team, and again led the team in blocks with 1.56 per game. He shot a team-best .579 from the floor, and his .618 [[field goal percentage]] in league games led the Atlantic 10. In addition, he led the team and finished third in the Atlantic 10 in rebounding with 9.0 rebounds per game. He had 14 double-doubles on the season. In the Owls' game against [[Lafayette Leopards|Lafayette]], Allen broke his thumb and was forced to miss the next game against [[Buffalo Bulls men's basketball|Buffalo]]. His season-high 23 points came on February 8, when the Owls defeated the [[Rhode Island Rams]] 68–62; Allen also had 13 rebounds.{{cite news|url=https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290390218|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120714074841/https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290390218|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 14, 2012|title=Temple 68, Rhode Island 62|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 8, 2009|access-date=December 27, 2010}} The following day, Allen received his first [[Philadelphia Big 5]] player of the week honors. He would again be honored as Big 5 player of the week on February 23, following a 20-point and season-high 18 rebound performance against [[St. Bonaventure]].{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290530218|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090225081746/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290530218|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 25, 2009|title=Temple 70, St. Bonaventure 56|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 22, 2009|access-date=December 28, 2010}} At the end of the regular season, Allen was named to the All-Atlantic 10 Third Team and All-Atlantic 10 Defensive Team. He helped Temple to its second consecutive Atlantic 10 Tournament title and NCAA Tournament appearance. In the championship game over [[Duquesne Dukes men's basketball|Duquesne]], Allen contributed 10 points and 14 rebounds.{{cite news|url=https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290730218|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120717002300/https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=290730218|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 2009|access-date=January 11, 2011}} He posted 10 points and 11 rebounds against [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] in a [[2009 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2009 NCAA tournament]] round of 64 loss. ===Junior=== [[File:Lavoy Allen.jpg|thumb|right|Allen attempts a [[free throw]] on February 28, 2010, with [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]].]] Allen was a Preseason All-Atlantic 10 First Team selection in his junior year.{{cite web|url=http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/atl10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/MBBPre0910.pdf|title=2009-10 Atlantic 10 Men's 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121112092337/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/atl10/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/MBBPre0910.pdf|url-status=dead}} He averaged 11.5 points and 10.7 rebounds per game, becoming the first Temple player to average a double-double since [[Ollie Johnson (basketball, born 1949)|Ollie Johnson]] accomplished the feat in 1970–71.{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2010/news/story?id=5131161|title=Allen declares for draft|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=April 23, 2010|access-date=January 2, 2011}} Allen's 10.9 rebounds per game average in Atlantic 10 conference games was bested only by [[Fordham Rams|Fordham]]'s [[Chris Gaston]] and [[2009–10 Duquesne Dukes men's basketball team|Duquesne]]'s [[Damian Saunders]].{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/3/stat/rebounds/sort/avgRebounds/year/2010/atlantic-10-conference|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120708005125/http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/conferences/statistics/player/_/id/3/stat/rebounds/sort/avgRebounds/year/2010/atlantic-10-conference|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 8, 2012|title=Atlantic 10 Team Rebounds Statistics - 2009-10|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|access-date=April 28, 2011}} In addition, he led Temple in field goal percentage at .536. He scored 10 points and snatched 17 rebounds in the Owls' upset of #3 [[2009–10 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] on December 19.{{cite news|url=https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293470218|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715233250/https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=293470218|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 15, 2012|title=Fernandez drains 7 3-pointers to help Temple stun Villanova |agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=December 13, 2009|access-date=April 28, 2011}} In a 65–53 win over La Salle on February 28, 2010, Allen scored 17 points and grabbed 21 rebounds,{{cite news|url=https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300592325|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103112412/https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300592325|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 3, 2013|title=Fernandez scores 23; Allen has 17 points, 21 rebounds as Temple sends message|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=February 28, 2010|access-date=April 29, 2011}} a career high and the most by an Owl since [[Joe Newman (basketball player)|Joe Newman]] pulled down 24 on February 5, 1973. With the victory, Temple clinched the Philadelphia Big Five title with a perfect 4–0 record. Allen became the 46th Temple player to score 1,000 points in his career in a game against [[George Washington Colonials men's basketball|George Washington]]. This earned him Atlantic 10 (co-)player of the week honors for the week of March 7. Led by Allen, Temple enjoyed a 29–5 season, captured a share of the Atlantic 10 conference regular season championship with a 14–2 record, and culminated in a third consecutive [[2010 Atlantic 10 men's basketball tournament|Atlantic 10 conference tournament]] title and an automatic bid to the [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cite news|url=https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300730218|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120720205638/https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300730218|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 20, 2012|title=Temple holds off Richmond rally to claim another A-10 championship|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 14, 2010|access-date=April 29, 2011}} In the NCAA Tournament, Temple was seeded fifth and matched up with 12 seed [[2009–10 Cornell Big Red men's basketball team|Cornell]] in the first round. Allen had 11 points, but his Owls were upset by the Big Red 78–65.{{cite news|url=https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300780218|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103184805/https://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300780218|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 3, 2013|title=Cornell builds big lead, dominates Temple in first-round upset|agency=[[Associated Press]]|work=[[ESPN]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|date=March 19, 2010|access-date=April 30, 2011}} He declared for early entry in the draft, but did not hire an [[sports agent|agent]]. After one workout with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], Allen was told to return to school to work on his offensive game.{{cite magazine|first=Ted|last=Keith|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1177621/index.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104060348/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1177621/index.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 4, 2012|title=20 Temple Owls|access-date=April 30, 2011|date=November 22, 2010|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|publisher=[[Time Inc.]]}} On May 8, Allen officially pulled his name out of consideration for the draft. He did so on the final day allowed by the NCAA to ensure collegiate eligibility.{{cite news|first=Keith|last=Tatum|url=http://articles.philly.com/2010-05-09/sports/24958523_1_owls-lavoy-allen-temple|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120503102706/http://articles.philly.com/2010-05-09/sports/24958523_1_owls-lavoy-allen-temple|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 3, 2012|title=Lavoy Allen out of NBA draft|access-date=April 30, 2011|date=May 9, 2010|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com}} ===Senior=== Allen was named to the 20-man USA Select team, which played with and against the USA National team from July 19-24.{{cite news|first=Phil|last=Jasner|url=http://articles.philly.com/2010-07-09/sports/24967473_1_76ers-andre-iguodala-nate-mcmillan-duke-s-mike-krzyzewski|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120503102711/http://articles.philly.com/2010-07-09/sports/24967473_1_76ers-andre-iguodala-nate-mcmillan-duke-s-mike-krzyzewski|url-status=dead|archive-date=May 3, 2012|title=Temple's Allen, other locals to play for USA select team|work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=July 9, 2010 |access-date=April 30, 2011}} Prior to his senior campaign, he was on the preseason [[John R. Wooden Award]] and [[Naismith College Player of the Year]] watchlists.{{cite web|url=http://www.woodenaward.com/?p=861|title=2010-2011 Men's Preseason Top 50 List|work=[[John R. news|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/nba/2012/01/seeing-sixers/|first=Tzvi|last=Twersky|title=Seeing Sixe(r)s|work=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]]|access-date=August 12, 2012|date=January 9, 2012}} He Allen responded by scoring 10 points on 5–5 shooting and pulling down six rebounds en route to a 103–83 victory.{{cite news|url=http://www.buckslocalnews.com/articles/2012/01/24/yardley_news/sports/doc4f1ecca3786ce880110610.txt?viewmode=fullstory|first=Steve|last=Sherman|title=NBA: Lavoy Allen reaches double figures in Philadelphia 76ers win over Washington Wizards|work=Bucks Local News|access-date=August 12, 2012|date=January 24, 2012}} He recorded a season-high 15 points on February 1 against the [[Chicago Bulls]], and a season-high 12 rebounds against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] on April 25.{{cite news|title=Andre Iguodala scores 19 points, leads 76ers past Bulls|url=https://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320201020|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130124050116/https://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320201020|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 24, 2013|access-date=August 13, 2012|work=[[ESPN]]|date=February 1, 2012|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures}}{{cite news|first=Bob|last=Cooney|url=https://www.philly.com/philly/sports/homepage/20120427_XXXX.html|title=Allen may be middle man|work=[[Philadelphia Daily News]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=April 27, 2012|access-date=August 14, 2012}} In 41 regular season games and 15 as a starter, Allen averaged 4.1 points and 4.2 rebounds per game. Allen raised his averages in the playoffs to 6.3 points and 4.9 rebounds per game. Coach [[Doug Collins (basketball)|Doug Collins]] named him the starting center in the playoff opener against the Bulls.{{cite news|first=Bob|last=Cooney|url=https://www.philly.com/philly/sports/sportsweek/20120427_Collins__players_back_on_same_page_as_playoffs_begin.html|title=Collins, players back on same page as playoffs begin|work=[[Philadelphia Daily News]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=April 28, 2012|access-date=August 15, 2012}} In his first playoff game, Allen sprained his thumb, but the injury was not considered severe.{{cite news|title=Derrick Rose tears ACL late in Bulls' Game 1 win over 76ers|url=https://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320428004|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130124055742/https://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320428004|url-status=dead|archive-date=January 24, 2013|access-date=August 15, 2012|work=[[ESPN]]|date=April 28, 2012|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures}} In Game 2 of the series, he nearly posted a double double with 11 points and nine rebounds.{{cite news|first=John|last=Mitchell|url=https://www.philly.com/philly/sports/sixers/20120503_Bulls_determined_to_regain_tough_defense.html|title=Bulls determined to regain tough defense|work=[[Philadelphia Inquirer]]|publisher=Philly.com|date=May 3, 2012|access-date=August 15, 2012}} The 76ers advanced past the Bulls to face the [[Boston Celtics]] in the conference semifinals. Allen hit the "shot of [his] life" to help the 76ers defeat the Celtics 82–81 in the second game of the series. With the score tied and four minutes left, [[Andre Iguodala]] passed the ball to Allen, who hit a 22-foot jumper as the shot clock expired. He earned his postseason minutes partially because of his ability to guard Celtics star [[Kevin Garnett]].{{cite news|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/nba/story/2012-05-15/philadelphia-76ers-boston-celtics-nba-playoffs-game-2-lavoy-allen-jrue-holiday|title=Lavoy Allen hits 'shot of his life', 76ers win Game 1 ===Northern Arizona Suns (2018)=== Allen signed with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] in China in November 2017 but never joined the team. In February 2018 he was picked up by the [[Northern Arizona Suns]] of the [[NBA G League]]. In his second game on February 11, Allen had 14 points and 12 rebounds. He followed up this performance with 12 points and 12 rebounds the next game.
